messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: High-priority incident triggered (PD #INC-7219). Metric: host-gpu-io_errors > 5/min across nodes in us-central1-a/b. Paging: @sre-mike. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-host-instability

sre-mike: acked. I'm oncall. Initial question: any customer-facing errors? Are model serving requests failing or just degraded latency?

alice: seeing elevated tail latency for a small subset of pods on dedicated pools -> 10-20% 95th token latency spikes, a few OOM-like disconnects. No large error spike in API 5xxs yet.

emma: telemetry shows repeated kernel AER PCIe errors on host-0[23-26]. GCE host logs show GPU driver resets ~2026-04-22T02:18Z onwards. Posting snippets below.

emma: ```
[ 1023.845678] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple/unexpected error, PCIe AER detected
[ 1023.846001] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1023.846210] nvidia: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1024.123456] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, pid 1234, gpu 0, TA context
```

raj: that Xid 79 is a GPU page fault / memory access error - commonly shows up with ECC or PCIe issues. Can we get nvidia-smi -q and dmesg for the node?

infra-liz: I've grabbed logs, uploading to GCS: gs://redwood-logs/incidents/2001234567/host-023/ (link restricted) - includes dmesg, kernel, gcp serial console. Also attached hypervisor events showing noisy neighbor CPU steal in same AZ host group.

ops-bot: NOTE: moved affected instances to maintenance group, started cordon of pod nodes in k8s cluster redwood-dedicated-uscent. Command used: kubectl cordon gpu-host-023 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-host-023

sre-mike: thanks. Emma/infra-liz - timeline so far: 02:17Z first PCIe AER on host-023, 02:18Z GPU reset and model worker reconnects, 02:23Z repeated resets on hosts 023/024/025, 02:41Z autoscale triggered to cover backfilled requests. Customer impact: some dedicated customers saw transient token truncation / reconnects; support triage is contacting impacted tenant IDs.

alice: quick note: we saw increased preemptible eviction errors on backfill nodes ~02:30Z but that's separate - not correlated to PCIe resets.

emma: digging into serial console, I see NVME controller errors just prior to PCIe AERs on one host. Possible root cause chain: storage IO blowup -> PCIe error propagation -> GPU bus fault. Example from serial: ```
Mar 22 02:17:54 host kernel: nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout
Mar 22 02:17:54 host kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
Mar 22 02:17:55 host kernel: NVRM: Xid 79
```

raj: hypothesis list so far (tagging): H1: underlying PCIe fabric instability (hardware ECC/slot issues). H2: noisy neighbor generating excess PCIe or NVMe IO causing timeouts. H3: GPU driver regression + kernel bug exposing ECC page faults. H4: GCP host firmware bug triggered by NVMe condition.

sre-mike: good. Let's track hypotheses inline. For each hypothesis we need evidence requests and owners.

sre-mike: H1 owner: infra-liz. Evidence needed: hardware ECC counters, pcie_ecrc stats, and any ECC counts from nvidia-smi -q.

infra-liz: on it. Pasting nvidia-smi ECC section: ```
=============== NVSMI LOG ===============
GPU 00000000:03:00.0
    FB Memory ECC errors
        Volatile: 0
        Aggregate: 3
    L2 Cache ECC errors
        Volatile: 1
        Aggregate: 7
```

infra-liz: Also checked pcie link status: link speed dropped to x4 for ~30s before resets in one host, others stayed at x16.

sre-mike: H2 (noisy neighbor) owner: alice. Evidence: hypervisor CPU steal, I/O wait in host metrics, tenant colocation metadata, and GCE activity logs.

alice: verified steal spikes on host-024 at 02:16-02:20Z (20-30% SOFTIRQ/steal). We have a colocated non-GPU workload on the same host group running heavy NVMe IO snapshots (customer backup job scheduled). I've flagged the tenant and asked GCP support to throttle.

emma: H3 (driver) owner: raj. Evidence: compare our driver version to known issue list, check recent kernel/driver rollout. GPU driver: 525.85.05, kernel: 5.15.0-1053-gcp. No recent driver rollouts in past 7 days. Searching internal bug DB for Xid 79 + driver 525 -> nothing recent.

raj: H4 (firmware) owner: infra-liz / escalation to GCP. Evidence: host firmware versions, NVMe firmware, and any platform maintenance windows.

ops-bot: ACTION: created ticket GCP-INC-93421 with priority P2. Contact: GCP hardware support assigned (case link internal). Please add logs to the case.

sre-mike: mitigation steps executed: 1) cordoned affected nodes, 2) migrated high-risk customers to dedicated standby hosts, 3) increased caching TTL for in-flight requests to reduce repeat compute, 4) temporarily disabled model quantization fallback on affected pool (to avoid small-memory allocations). Any reversions?

alice: we also rolled an emergency kernel param bump to increase PCIe AER logging and prevent immediate reset (sysctl pcie_aspm=off) — rolled to cordoned nodes only. Need infra-liz signoff to roll cluster-wide.

infra-liz: don't roll cluster-wide yet. Need more evidence — the lockdown increased stability on two hosts but not on host-025. Host-025 still has intermittent Xid 79 every ~10-15 minutes.

emma: sharing a full timeline and log bundle in the incident folder with annotated events. Also created a minimal repro job that submits continuous small NVMe reads to a test instance in the same AZ to try to reproduce. Link: gs://redwood-logs/incidents/2001234567/repro/

raj: quick check: does telemetry show elevated ECC counts correlating with the NVMe errors? If ECC counters increment only after NVMe events, that suggests propagation.

infra-liz: ECC counters appear to climb after NVMe error bursts. Preliminary correlation ~+2 ECC errs within 30s after NVMe I/O timeout.

sre-mike: next steps (owners): infra-liz -> escalate to GCP with firmware/host-level evidence (deadline +2h). alice -> coordinate with support to throttle/evict noisy tenant (deadline +1h). raj -> reproduce locally and search for driver regressions (deadline +3h). emma -> assemble timeline and customer impact list, liaise with support reps for comms (deadline +30m).

alice: support update: notified affected customers list and created a short incident blurb for status.redwood.ai. No public incident page yet, will wait for impact quantification.

ops-bot: RUNBOOK NOTE: follow post-incident checklist: collect kernel-oom logs, nv-host logs, dmesg, pcie_aer, lspci -vvv and attach to RCA.

sre-mike: logging an interim summary for handoff to the next shift: multiple hosts in us-central experienced PCIe AERs with downstream GPU resets starting 02:17Z, correlated NVMe IO timeouts and transient link speed drops; noisy neighbor backup job found colocated; mitigation included cordon/drain, tenant throttle, and temporary kernel param adjustments. Ongoing: GCP hardware case open. Next oncall please prioritize GCP case and customer comms.

infra-liz: adding GCP case number to thread once available. Also scheduling a hardware replacement window for host-025 pending support confirmation.

emma: from an ops perspective, observed that model worker side gracefully reconnected in ~15-30s on most resets; request-level timeouts were sticky for a few customers - support is patching those.

raj: I'll run a driver binary with extra debug in a canary to capture any reproducible memory access fault patterns. If I can reproduce with our repro job, we can rule out purely hardware.

sre-mike: thanks all. I'm leaving this as the active incident thread. Next update expected in 30m or on escalation events. If GCP provides root cause or hardware replacement ETA, paste here and we'll update customer comms. :thumbsup:
